archetype.name: Playoff Team (offense-first)
archetype.definition: An Indiana side whose guard-driven, efficient half-court offense projects comfortably into the East's playoff field, while a league-average defense keeps it below the true contenders for now.

report.headline: Haliburton-led offense is back near the top; the defense is still unproven.
report.take:
Indiana is three games removed from a 19-63 season in which its offense ranked 29th, and it already looks like a different team. The Pacers are 2-1 with a Net Rtg of 4.5 (10th) and an ORtg of 117.2 (9th). The site has them 10th of 30. That is closer to the 50-32 team of 2024-25, which ranked 9th on offense and 13th on defense, than to anything from last year. The record isn't flattering them either: W vs Pt Diff is 0, and the margin implies exactly the two wins they have.

The engine is the backcourt, graded A-. Tyrese Haliburton sits 7th on the point guard tab with a BPM of 6 and an On-Off of 18.1. Andrew Nembhard is shooting a 70 TS % beside him. Behind them, Pascal Siakam is carrying a heavy 31.5 USG % at a 61.4 TS %, and Obi Toppin has been the most efficient scorer on the roster at 72.8. Together that produces an eFG % of 58.4, 2nd in the league. It is built on finishing rather than a hot three-point streak: the 3P % of 35.2 ranks only 11th, and the team takes fewer threes than the league average.

The weak spot is the defense. A DRtg of 112.7 ranks 16th and sits almost exactly on the league average. The one standout number underneath it, opponents shooting 57.9 at the rim (4th), sits on top of the 28th-ranked Opp Rim Rate. Indiana is letting teams into the paint more than almost anyone and has gotten fortunate when they arrive. In every season on the sheet, opponents finished at the rim in the mid-60s, so expect that figure to climb. The wings, graded C, are a second leak: Kelly Oubre Jr. has an On-Off of -15.6 at a 43 TS %.

Three games are a thin sample, and the blowout loss to Dallas, 105-121, shows how quickly it can turn. Even so, the shape is believable because this franchise has played this way before. A top-10 offense driven by its point guard, with a defense that has to hold the middle, is a playoff profile in this conference. Whether it becomes more than that depends on the frontcourt and wing defense, not the shooting.

strengths.title: Elite shot quality and finishing
strengths.body: Indiana's eFG % of 58.4 ranks 2nd and its TS % of 61.1 ranks 3rd, well clear of the league average. The efficiency comes mostly from inside the arc and from guard-created looks, since its 3P % is merely good. The 2023-24 team posted a 57.8 eFG %, so this is a repeatable style rather than a fluke. Expect some cooling, but a top-10 offense should hold.

strengths.title: Haliburton's backcourt drives everything
strengths.body: The backcourt grades A-, and Haliburton's On-Off of 18.1 and BPM of 6 show how much the team depends on him. Nembhard's 70 TS % and On-Off of 11.2 make the starting guard pair the clearest plus on the roster. They have held their own at the other end too: opposing point guards have produced well under their usual output. With the backcourt this dominant, its health is the season's biggest dependency.

strengths.title: Toppin's efficient scoring punch
strengths.body: Obi Toppin ranks 13th on the power forward tab, with a 72.8 TS %, a BPM of 4.7 and 8 threes in limited minutes. That gives the frontcourt a second scorer next to Siakam's high-usage game. His shooting will come down from this level, but a stretch big who finishes is a genuine role.

concerns.title: Rim defense numbers won't hold
concerns.body: Opponents are taking a large share of their shots at the rim, ranked 28th by Opp Rim Rate, yet converting only 57.9 there, far below the league average. Every season in the sheet's history has opponents finishing in the mid-60s at the rim against Indiana, including 66 last year. When that conversion rate normalizes while teams keep attacking the paint, a DRtg already around league average will slide.

concerns.title: Wing rotation is a hole
concerns.body: The wings grade C. Oubre's 43 TS % and On-Off of -15.6, along with Aaron Nesmith's BPM of -8.5, mean the minutes between the guards and Siakam are losing ground. Opposing small forwards account for a much larger share of points against Indiana than the league norm. That partly reflects the high-volume forwards it has faced, since those players fell short of their own averages. Jalen Slawson's strong early minutes are the one internal fix to watch.

concerns.title: Few extra possessions, thin frontcourt
concerns.body: Indiana ranks 29th in ORB % and 20th in Opp TOV %, so it neither creates second chances nor forces many turnovers. The frontcourt grades C-. Ivica Zubac, its center, is day-to-day with an On-Off of -16.7, and Jarace Walker has struggled badly. The low offensive-rebounding rate matches the franchise's history and is likely a style choice, but it leaves no margin on cold shooting nights like the Dallas loss.

trend.note: Measured against a 19-63 season with the 29th-ranked offense, three games of top-10 Net Rtg is a sharp step up. Within this season the path has been uneven: a close win at New Orleans, a heavy home loss to Dallas, then a 136-109 rout at Brooklyn.

weekAhead.headline: Three winless opponents, then Philadelphia and a back-to-back finish
weekAhead.body:
Five games in eight days, and the middle of the week is soft. Milwaukee, Miami and Brooklyn are a combined winless start. All three rank in the bottom third by DRtg, and Miami and Brooklyn rank near the bottom in Opp 3P % and Opp eFG %. Indiana already scored 136 on Brooklyn, and an efficient offense should feast on defenses like these. Anything short of three wins from those games would be a red flag.

The bookends are the test. Philadelphia is 3-1 with the 5th-ranked DRtg, a real check on Indiana's shot-making, though its 28th-ranked offense limits how much it can punish the Pacers back. Atlanta closes the week on the second night of a home back-to-back with a Net Rtg of 15.4, 3rd in the league, and the 4th-ranked offense. That game is the best read yet on whether Indiana's defense holds up against quality.

keyMatchups.title: Siakam against Atlanta's power forwards
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta has allowed 33.67 points a game to power forwards, 28th in the league and well above those players' norms, and its frontcourt grades D-. Siakam, at a 31.5 USG %, is the natural pressure point. Exploiting that mismatch is Indiana's best route to beating a top-three Net Rtg team on tired legs.

keyMatchups.title: Pacers offense versus Philadelphia's defense
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia's DRtg of 102.5 ranks 5th, a far tougher test than anything else this week. Its offense is 28th by ORtg, and it ranks last in REB % and ORB %. That last-place rebounding takes away one of Indiana's usual weaknesses. Expect a lower-scoring game decided by who makes shots.

keyMatchups.title: Soft middle of the schedule
keyMatchups.body: Milwaukee (DRtg 122, 26th), Miami (Opp 3P % of 42, 30th) and Brooklyn (Opp eFG % of 60.7, 29th) have all struggled to defend. Milwaukee also ranks last in Opp TOV %, so Indiana's ball security should hold. These games should keep the offense's numbers inflated.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Zubac plays, and whether opponents keep missing at the rim as they keep attacking it, especially Atlanta on the back-to-back.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the part to trust. The style matches the 2023-24 and 2024-25 teams, its efficiency comes from finishing rather than a three-point spike, and the backcourt grades as one of the league's best. I'd project an ORtg in the 114-118 range. That is likely a step down from the current 117.2, but still clearly above average. The record so far matches the margin, so there is no close-game luck to give back.

The defense will likely regress. Opponents finishing at the rim this poorly while getting there this often doesn't last, and the wing rotation is a minus. A Net Rtg between roughly 0 and 4 and 41-49 wins is the realistic band: a solid playoff team, short of contender status unless the wing and frontcourt defense improves. The 55-win pace on the sheet is a three-game artifact.
swingFactors: Opponent rim finishing regressing toward past seasons
Whether the wing minutes stop bleeding points

confidence.note: Three games; individual On-Off and rim numbers are especially noisy.
